RING SURFACE CRITERIA & FIDELITY

Constructed according to International Sumo Robot Rules (All-Japan / IEEE Chapter standard). The arena is fabricated from high-density matte MDF wood with non-reflective polyurethane coating; non-magnetic surface calibrated for silicone/rubber tire traction.

Ring Diameter & Core154.0 cm (±1.0 cm) • 25.0 mm Matte Black High-Density MDF
Surface CoatingPolyurethane non-reflective seal (Non-magnetic substrate)
Tawara Border (White Line)5.0 cm width, polyurethane white coat
Starting Lines (Shikiri-sen)2.0 x 20.0 cm, 10.0 cm apart from center
Ring Elevation5.0 cm off floor level with empty fall zone
Fall-Out Demarcation100.0 cm perimeter soft foam cushion
Optical Reflection SpecMatte Black: ≤ 8% • White Border: ≥ 88%

CHAMPIONSHIP SCHEDULE // 日程

OFFICIAL TOURNAMENT STAGES & BOUT CADENCE
STAGE 01 // HOMOLOGATION

Homologation

Volumetric box fit check, tare weight measurement, blade edge radius inspection, and autonomous failsafe verification. Only homologated robots enter the bout draw.

STATUS: [MANDATORY GATEWAY]
STAGE 02 // POINT PHASE

Phase One Matches

Point-based round-robin pools. Best 2 out of 3 bouts, Yuhkoh points decide the table. The top robots from each pool advance to the knockout stage.

STATUS: [SIMULTANEOUS RINGS A/B]
STAGE 03 // KNOCKOUT

Knockout Stage

Single elimination bracket. 3-minute pit windows between bouts for battery swaps, tyre cleaning, and calibration adjustments.

STATUS: [ELIMINATION BRACKET]
STAGE 04 // FINAL

Grand Final & Honors

Center ring main event with elevated spectator stands. Valuable prizes and championship honors for the winners, including the Roboko Katana Trophy and IEEE Laurels.

STATUS: [TROPHY CEREMONY]

100% FREE PARTICIPATION & ADMISSION

No registration charges or spectator fees. Every qualified robotics squad receives full paddock workbench access, scrutineering certification, and arena bout slots free of charge.

THE STUDENT BRANCH

Roboko is organized by the IEEE student branch of ENP — the Ecole Nationale Polytechnique in El Harrach, Algiers — part of the international IEEE organization.

Founded in 2019, the branch runs events, activities, and workshops across various domains. The tournament returns for its 3rd edition.

SCRUTINEERING PROTOCOLS // 審査規約

helpHow does a Sumo Robot battle work?

Two robots compete in a ring, aiming to push their opponent out while staying inside the boundaries.

memoryWhat type of robots are allowed?

Robots must comply with RoboKO’s technical specifications, dimensions, and competition rules.

groupsIs the competition individual or team-based?

Participants can compete in teams, according to the competition’s registration guidelines.

timerHow long does each robot battle last?

Each battle follows the competition’s official timing rules, with robots competing to outmaneuver and push their opponents out of the ring.
